threshold_note: 0.5 = convention used elsewhere in the paper; 0.15 = deployed BLOCK_THRESHOLD (continuous_waf.py). Neither was tuned on the data used here.

not_included.Edge-IIoTset: Not attempted: distributed through IEEE DataPort / Kaggle (account-gated as far as known, not a plain download), and its released tables are network-flow features rather than raw HTTP payload strings, so the payload featuriser would need a different pipeline. Listed as future work.
not_included.other_IoT_sets: None cheaply downloadable with raw HTTP payloads were found.

csic2010.label_note: CSIC 'anomalous' = all attack types in the dataset (SQLi, XSS, buffer overflow, CRLF, path traversal, info gathering, parameter tampering ...). Many are not payload-signature attacks; recall is NOT attack-family recall. Not stratified by sub-type (no sub-type labels in file).

loco.note: pooled centralised training with the shipped featuriser, augmentation and SGD hyper-parameters; held-out strings exactly de-duplicated from training within their family; recall/FPR use ONE random augmentation per held-out payload per seed; bootstrap CI over payloads of the seed-averaged outcome. AUC = held-out vs in-distribution test (30% splits) of the opposite class, mean and min/max over seeds.

synthetic_benign.note: synthetic, generated deterministically (seed 2024) by synth_benign(); each string scored as ONE context with the shipped model. 'hard_negatives_*' (SQL words / markup / operators in prose) are reported separately and excluded from the headline aggregate.
